q.t: Fill in: The dog ___ loudly.
q.e: One dog → singular verb (with -s).

q.t: Fill in: The children ___ in the garden.
q.e: ‘children’ is plural → are.

q.t: Fill in: She ___ a new bicycle.
q.e: She (singular) → has.

q.t: Fill in: Riya and Sam ___ best friends.
q.e: Two subjects joined by ‘and’ → plural.

q.t: Fill in: My brother ___ in Delhi.
q.e: Singular subject → lives.

q.t: Fill in: There ___ a cat on the wall.
q.e: The real subject (a cat) comes after ‘there’; it is singular → is.

q.t: Fill in: There ___ many books on the shelf.
q.e: The real subject is ‘many books’ (plural) → are.

q.t: Fill in: Everyone ___ happy today.
q.e: everyone = every single one → singular.

q.t: Fill in: The birds ___ south in winter.
q.e: Plural subject → plural verb (no -s).

q.t: Fill in: He ___ not like spinach.
q.e: He (singular) → does.

q.t: Fill in: The box of pencils ___ on the desk.
q.e: The subject is ‘box’; ‘of pencils’ only describes it.

q.t: Fill in: One of my friends ___ a doctor.
q.e: The subject is ‘one’ → singular.

q.t: Fill in: Each of the students ___ a laptop.
q.e: ‘Each’ is singular, whatever comes after ‘of’.

q.t: Fill in: Neither Ravi nor his sisters ___ coming.
q.e: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: sisters → are.

q.t: Fill in: Either the students or the teacher ___ responsible.
q.e: Nearer subject is ‘the teacher’ → singular.

q.t: Fill in: The news ___ very good.
q.e: ‘news’ is singular despite the -s.

q.t: Fill in: My new trousers ___ too long.
q.e: ‘trousers’ is always plural.

q.t: Fill in: The furniture in this room ___ old.
q.e: ‘furniture’ is uncountable → singular.

q.t: Fill in: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
q.e: The name of one subject → singular.

q.t: Fill in: The police ___ arrested the thief.
q.e: ‘police’ is always treated as plural.

q.t: Fill in: The principal, along with the teachers, ___ attending the meeting.
q.e: ‘along with the teachers’ does not add to the subject. The subject is ‘the principal’ → is.

q.t: Fill in: Bread and butter ___ my favourite breakfast.
q.e: Bread and butter is one dish, one idea → singular.

q.t: Fill in: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
q.e: A distance thought of as one amount → singular.

q.t: Fill in: The number of students in the class ___ forty.
q.e: ‘The number’ is one figure → singular.

q.t: Fill in: A number of students ___ absent today.
q.e: ‘A number of’ means ‘many’ → plural.

q.t: Fill in: A pair of shoes ___ lying under the bed.
q.e: The subject is ‘pair’ (one) → singular.

q.t: Fill in: The team ___ won the cup.
q.e: The team acting as one unit → singular.

q.t: Fill in: Not only the players but also the coach ___ happy.
q.e: With not only … but also, agree with the nearer subject: the coach → was.

q.t: Find the error: The quality of these mangoes are excellent.
q.e: The subject is ‘quality’ (singular); ‘of these mangoes’ only describes it.

q.t: Fill in: Five hundred rupees ___ too much for this shirt.
q.e: A sum of money as one amount → singular.

q.t: Fill in: Many a student ___ failed this test.
q.e: ‘Many a’ + singular noun takes a singular verb.

q.t: Fill in: She is one of the girls who ___ in the choir.
q.e: ‘who’ refers to ‘the girls’ (plural) — the girls sing, and she is one of them.

q.t: Fill in: She is the only one of the girls who ___ the violin.
q.e: Now ‘who’ refers to ‘the only one’ (singular) → plays.

q.t: Fill in: The jury ___ divided in their opinions.
q.e: Members acting separately (divided, their) → plural.

q.t: Fill in: The secretary and treasurer ___ arrived. (one person holding both jobs)
q.e: One ‘the’ for both titles = one person → singular.

q.t: Fill in: Neither of the answers ___ correct.
q.e: ‘Neither’ is singular, even with ‘of the answers’.

q.t: Fill in: “Gulliver's Travels” ___ a famous book.
q.e: The title of one book → singular.

q.t: Find the error: Either you or he are to blame.
q.e: Agree with the nearer subject ‘he’ → is.

q.t: Find the error: The cattle is grazing in the field.
q.e: ‘cattle’ is always plural.

q.t: Fill in: Physics as well as chemistry ___ taught by Mr Rao.
q.e: ‘as well as chemistry’ does not add to the subject; ‘Physics’ (one subject) → is.
